### CLI Onboarding and Setup

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/start/wizard.md

Run these commands to start the guided terminal setup or the configuration-only baseline variant.

```bash
openclaw onboard
```

```bash
openclaw setup
```

```bash
openclaw onboard --classic
```

--------------------------------

### Quickstart with Peekaboo CLI

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/skills/peekaboo/SKILL.md

Basic commands to get started with Peekaboo, including checking permissions, listing applications, taking a screenshot, clicking an element, and typing text.

```bash
peekaboo permissions
peekaboo list apps --json
peekaboo see --annotate --path /tmp/peekaboo-see.png
peekaboo click --on B1
peekaboo type "Hello" --return
```

--------------------------------

### Initialize Feishu Channel Setup

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/channels/feishu.md

Starts the interactive wizard to install the Feishu plugin and configure App ID/Secret or QR-based authentication.

```bash
openclaw channels login --channel feishu
```

--------------------------------

### Initialize and Start OpenClaw Development Loop

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/README.md

Clone the repository and perform initial setup including dependency installation and workspace configuration. Use the watch command to auto-reload the gateway on source changes.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
cd openclaw

pnpm install

# First run only (or after resetting local OpenClaw config/workspace)
pnpm openclaw setup

# Optional: prebuild Control UI before first startup
pnpm ui:build

# Dev loop (auto-reload on source/config changes)
pnpm gateway:watch
```

--------------------------------

### Interactive Configuration Wizards

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/gateway/configuration.md

Guided flows for initial setup and configuration updates. Use onboard for first-time setup and configure for wizard-based edits.

```bash
openclaw onboard       # full onboarding flow
openclaw configure     # config wizard
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Wizard Setup and Metadata

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md

Manage behavior and metadata for CLI guided setup flows. Controls discovery consent and application recommendations during onboarding.

```json5
{
  wizard: {
    accessMode: "full",
    appRecommendations: true,
    lastRunAt: "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    lastRunVersion: "2026.1.4",
    lastRunCommit: "abc1234",
    lastRunCommand: "configure",
    lastRunMode: "local",
    securityAcknowledgedAt: "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  },
}
```

```bash
clawdock-start
```


### Install OpenClaw and run onboarding

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/macos-vm.md

Installs the latest version of OpenClaw globally and initiates the daemon installation and provider setup.

```bash
npm install -g openclaw@latest
openclaw onboard --install-daemon
```

--------------------------------

### Initialize and manage OpenClaw setup

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/web/tui.md

Commands to start the interactive setup assistant or execute specific configuration tasks. Requires approval for persistent writes unless the --yes flag is provided.

```bash
openclaw setup                       # start interactively
openclaw setup -m "status"           # run one request and exit
openclaw setup -m "set default model openai/gpt-5.2" --yes   # apply a config write
```

--------------------------------

### Install and initialize Honcho plugin via CLI

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/concepts/memory-honcho.md

Run these commands to install the package and perform initial setup. The setup process includes credential configuration and optional migration of existing memory files.

```bash
openclaw plugins install @honcho-ai/openclaw-honcho
openclaw honcho setup
openclaw gateway --force
```

### Install OpenClaw with Specific Method

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/help/faq-first-run.md

Use the installation script with the --install-method flag to force a git or npm setup. This is useful for initial provisioning on a new machine.

```bash
curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --install-method git
```

```bash
curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --install-method npm
```

```bash
curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash
openclaw onboard --install-daemon
```

--------------------------------

### Configure OpenClaw Gateway, Cron, and Webhooks

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/gateway/configuration-examples.md

Comprehensive example for setting up background jobs, Gmail webhooks, and gateway networking. Includes settings for Tailscale integration and skill installation.

```json5
// Cron jobs
  cron: {
    enabled: true,
    store: "~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json",
    maxConcurrentRuns: 8, // default; cron dispatch + isolated cron agent-turn execution
    sessionRetention: "24h",
  },

  // Webhooks
  hooks: {
    enabled: true,
    path: "/hooks",
    token: "shared-secret",
    presets: ["gmail"],
    transformsDir: "~/.openclaw/hooks/transforms",
    mappings: [
      {
        id: "gmail-hook",
        match: { path: "gmail" },
        action: "agent",
        wakeMode: "now",
        name: "Gmail",
        sessionKey: "hook:gmail:{{messages[0].id}}",
        messageTemplate: "From: {{messages[0].from}}\nSubject: {{messages[0].subject}}",
        textTemplate: "{{messages[0].snippet}}",
        deliver: true,
        channel: "last",
        to: "+15555550123",
        thinking: "low",
        timeoutSeconds: 300,
        transform: {
          module: "gmail.js",
          export: "transformGmail",
        },
      },
    ],
    gmail: {
      account: "openclaw@gmail.com",
      label: "INBOX",
      topic: "projects/<project-id>/topics/gog-gmail-watch",
      subscription: "gog-gmail-watch-push",
      pushToken: "shared-push-token",
      hookUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:18789/hooks/gmail",
      includeBody: true,
      maxBytes: 20000,
      renewEveryMinutes: 720,
      serve: { bind: "127.0.0.1", port: 8788, path: "/" },
      tailscale: { mode: "funnel", path: "/gmail-pubsub" },
    },
  },

  // Gateway + networking
  gateway: {
    mode: "local",
    port: 18789,
    bind: "loopback",
    controlUi: { enabled: true, basePath: "/openclaw" },
    auth: {
      mode: "token",
      token: "gateway-token",
      allowTailscale: true,
    },
    tailscale: { mode: "serve", resetOnExit: false },
    remote: { url: "ws://gateway-host.ts.net:18789", token: "remote-token" },
    reload: { mode: "hybrid", debounceMs: 300 },
  },

  skills: {
    allowBundled: ["gemini", "peekaboo"],
    load: {
      extraDirs: ["~/Projects/agent-scripts/skills"],
      allowSymlinkTargets: ["~/Projects/agent-scripts/skills"],
    },
    install: {
      preferBrew: true,
      nodeManager: "npm", // npm | pnpm | yarn | bun
      allowUploadedArchives: false,
    },
    entries: {
      "image-lab": {
        enabled: true,
        apiKey: "GEMINI_KEY_HERE",
        env: { GEMINI_API_KEY: "GEMINI_KEY_HERE" },
      },
      peekaboo: { enabled: true },
    },
  },
}
```

--------------------------------

### General openclaw config command examples

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/cli/config.md

Overview of common configuration tasks including file location, guided setup, getting/setting values, patching, and validation.

```bash
openclaw config file
openclaw config --section model
openclaw config --section gateway --section daemon
openclaw config schema
openclaw config get browser.executablePath
openclaw config set browser.executablePath "/usr/bin/google-chrome"
openclaw config set browser.profiles.work.executablePath "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome"
openclaw config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.every "2h"
openclaw config set 'agents.list[0].tools.exec.node' "node-id-or-name"
openclaw config set agents.defaults.models '{"openai/gpt-5.4":{}}' --strict-json --merge
openclaw config set channels.discord.token --ref-provider default --ref-source env --ref-id DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
openclaw config set secrets.providers.vaultfile --provider-source file --provider-path /etc/openclaw/secrets.json --provider-mode json
openclaw config patch --file ./openclaw.patch.json5 --dry-run
openclaw config unset plugins.entries.brave.config.webSearch.apiKey
openclaw config set channels.discord.token --ref-provider default --ref-source env --ref-id DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN --dry-run
openclaw config validate
openclaw config validate --json
```

### Install OpenClaw without onboarding

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/index.md

Installs the software while bypassing the interactive onboarding setup.

```bash

```

```powershell
& ([scriptblock]::Create((iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1))) -NoOnboard
```

### Binary-backed Setup Helpers

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/plugins/sdk-setup.md

Helpers for managing setup logic that interacts with external binaries or requires delegation to heavier wizards.

```APIDOC
## Binary-backed Setup Helpers

### Description
Helpers for managing setup logic that interacts with external binaries or requires delegation.

### Functions
- **createDetectedBinaryStatus(...)** - Status blocks for binary detection.
- **createCliPathTextInput(...)** - Text input for file system paths.
- **createDelegatedSetupWizardStatusResolvers(...)** - Forwards status resolution to a heavier wizard lazily.
- **createDelegatedPrepare(...)** - Delegates preparation logic.
- **createDelegatedFinalize(...)** - Delegates finalization logic.
- **createDelegatedResolveConfigured(...)** - Delegates configuration resolution.
- **createDelegatedTextInputShouldPrompt(...)** - Delegates input prompting decisions.
```

--------------------------------

### createOptionalChannelSetupSurface

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/plugins/sdk-setup.md

Creates optional setup surfaces that only appear in specific contexts, returning both a setup adapter and wizard.

```APIDOC
## createOptionalChannelSetupSurface(options)

### Description
Generates an optional setup surface that fails closed on real config writes and includes documentation links.

### Parameters
- **options** (object)
  - **channel** (string) - Channel identifier.
  - **label** (string) - Display label.
  - **npmSpec** (string) - NPM package specification.
  - **docsPath** (string) - Path to documentation.

### Returns
- **setupAdapter** (object) - The generated setup adapter.
- **setupWizard** (object) - The generated setup wizard.
```

Run these commands to start the onboarding wizard or manage application recommendations. Use specific flags to control the UI mode, migration source, or remote connection settings.

### Run OpenClaw installer with verbose logging

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/help/faq-first-run.md

Add the --verbose flag to the installation script to troubleshoot issues or get more feedback. These variants cover standard, beta, and git-based installation methods.

```bash
curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --verbose
```

```bash
curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --beta --verbose
```

```bash
curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --install-method git --verbose
```

### Install plugins using marketplace shorthand

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/cli/plugins.md

Use the @ syntax to install plugins from marketplaces cached in the local registry at ~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json.

```bash
openclaw plugins marketplace list <marketplace-name>
openclaw plugins install <plugin-name>@<marketplace-name>
```

### Recommended Starter Configuration

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/gateway/configuration-examples.md

A standard setup defining agent identity, primary model selection, and specific message handling for group chats.

```json5
{
  agents: {
    defaults: {
      workspace: "~/.openclaw/workspace",
      model: { primary: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6" },
    },
    list: [
      {
        id: "main",
        identity: {
          name: "Clawd",
          theme: "helpful assistant",
          emoji: "🦞",
        },
      },
    ],
  },
  channels: {
    whatsapp: {
      allowFrom: ["+15555550123"],
      groups: { "*": { requireMention: true } },
    },
  },
  messages: {
    visibleReplies: "automatic",
    groupChat: {
      visibleReplies: "message_tool", // opt-in; visible output requires message(action=send)
      unmentionedInbound: "room_event",
    },
  },
}
```

--------------------------------

### Automated OpenClaw Installation via Shelley

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/exe-dev.md

Use this prompt with the Shelley agent to automate the installation, Nginx configuration, and setup of OpenClaw on an exe.dev VM.

```text
Set up OpenClaw (https://docs.openclaw.ai/install) on this VM. Use the non-interactive and accept-risk flags for openclaw onboarding. Add the supplied auth or token as needed. Configure nginx to forward from the default port 18789 to the root location on the default enabled site config, making sure to enable Websocket support. Pairing is done by "openclaw devices list" and "openclaw devices approve <request id>". Make sure the dashboard shows that OpenClaw's health is OK. exe.dev handles forwarding from port 8000 to port 80/443 and HTTPS for us, so the final "reachable" should be <vm-name>.exe.xyz, without port specification.
```

--------------------------------

### AI-Evaluated Discretion Condition Example

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/open-prose/skills/prose/compiler.md

This example demonstrates using discretion markers (`**...**`) for AI-evaluated conditions to guide session execution based on code analysis.

```prose
let analysis = session "Analyze the codebase"

if **the code has security vulnerabilities**:
  session "Fix security issues immediately"
    context: analysis
elif **the code has performance issues**:
  session "Optimize performance bottlenecks"
    context: analysis
else:
  session "Proceed with normal review"
    context: analysis
```

### OpenCode-Go Configuration Example

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/opencode-go.md

Configure the provider by setting the API key in the environment and specifying a default model.

```json5
{
  env: { OPENCODE_API_KEY: "YOUR_API_KEY_HERE" }, // pragma: allowlist secret
  agents: { defaults: { model: { primary: "opencode-go/kimi-k2.6" } } },
}
```

### Install Docker on Debian VM

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/gcp.md

Install Docker and add the current user to the docker group. This setup allows running containers without requiring sudo for every command.

```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y git curl ca-certificates
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
```

### Manage Gateway service lifecycle

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/cli/gateway.md

Standard commands to install, start, stop, and restart the Gateway service.

```bash
openclaw gateway install
openclaw gateway start
openclaw gateway stop
openclaw gateway restart
openclaw gateway uninstall
```

--------------------------------

### Example Music Generation Prompts

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/music-generation.md

Natural language descriptions used to guide the music generation process.

```text
Generate a cinematic piano track with soft strings and no vocals.
```

```text
Generate an energetic chiptune loop about launching a rocket at sunrise.
```

--------------------------------

### Configure DNS-SD discovery with openclaw dns setup

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/cli/dns.md

Plan or apply CoreDNS setup for unicast DNS-SD discovery. Use --domain to specify a custom domain and --apply to install or update the configuration on macOS.

```bash
openclaw dns setup
openclaw dns setup --domain openclaw.internal
openclaw dns setup --apply
```

--------------------------------

### Onboard Fal Provider via CLI

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/fal.md

Run this command to interactively set up the Fal API key and default model.

```bash
openclaw onboard --auth-choice fal-api-key
```

--------------------------------

### Onboard Runway Provider via CLI

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/runway.md

Run this command to initialize the Runway provider and set up the API key authentication.

```bash
openclaw onboard --auth-choice runway-api-key
```

--------------------------------

### Setup DNS Server on macOS Gateway

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/gateway/bonjour.md

Automate the installation and configuration of CoreDNS on macOS to serve discovery records over Tailscale.

```bash
openclaw dns setup --apply
```

--------------------------------

### Install OpenProse from Local Source

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/prose.md

Install the plugin directly from a local repository checkout path.

```bash
openclaw plugins install ./extensions/open-prose
```

--------------------------------

### Install MeowCaller CLI

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/channels/whatsapp.md

Build the reviewed branch of MeowCaller to ensure compatibility with the notify command and proper path setup.

```bash
git clone --branch feat/send-only-notify https://github.com/steipete/meowcaller.git
cd meowcaller
git checkout 752050471fc2bf7a8cdfbf7dbd3cd4e865d85d3f
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
go build -o "$HOME/.local/bin/meowcaller" ./cmd/meowcaller
```

--------------------------------

### Manual migration on existing setups

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/migrating-claude.md

Use the apply command directly to migrate into an existing installation, which supports the --overwrite flag.

```bash
openclaw migrate apply claude
```

```bash
--overwrite
```
